name: chess with a spellbinding king
description: Chess in which the king turns the enemy pieces that come too close. Any enemy piece other than the king that stands on one of the eight squares around your king can be moved by you, on your turn and as your move for that turn, the way it always moves: to an empty square, or onto one of its own side's pieces, which it then captures (never a king). It stays its owner's piece, and its owner can still move it too. So the classic mate, a queen beside the king with a second piece guarding her, stops working: the defender moves the queen away, or makes her take the piece that guards her. Mates have to be given from a distance, by pieces that stay out of the king's reach, and every piece that closes in on a king is a liability as well as a threat. A spellbound piece never castles, captures in passing or promotes, and you may not move it so that your own king is left in check.
